place.zh: 沂中医 · 城里的医院 · 十一月底
place.en: Yizhong · the hospital in town · late November

setup.zh: 「凑数的。」他背着人「闭关三日」，晨脉八十八，回了一个「好」，蹲完了。夜里尿成可乐色：横纹肌溶解。出院那天，阿禾的纸上三条。
setup.en: "Just making up the numbers." He trains three days in secret; morning pulse 88; he answers "OK" and finishes the squats anyway. That night his urine is cola: rhabdomyolysis. On discharge, three lines on Ahe's paper.

recap.zh: 练太猛，横纹肌溶解，住院三天；「数是你自己报的」——晨脉七十以下，才许摸球。
recap.en: Overtrained, rhabdomyolysis, three days in hospital; "you report the numbers yourself" — under seventy in the morning, then the ball.

zh: 晨脉回到七十以下，才许摸球。
en: Under seventy in the morning — then the ball.

story.zh:
十一月二十一日，小组赛第三轮。替补席上摆着一排纸杯，杯口朝下，杯底写着号——阿禾的规矩：谁上过场，下来喝水，就把自己那只翻过来。沈芒拄着拐坐在看台上数了两遍：十一只。他那只「0」，没摆上去。

散场时，马小宝晃过来，拿摇杯点了点他的拐：「零号。一队报十二个人，少一个报不上名——你就是来凑数的。」古籍部那一夜，两个人谁也没提。

这话一个字也没说错，所以格外疼。可疼完了，他心里竟悄悄松了一下：凑数的，没人看，不用站上罚球线。这一松，他自己也吓了一跳，赶紧按了回去。

那天夜里，老蔡的手机从上铺垂下来，屏幕停在一行字上：「少年闭关三日，出关连破两境。」

半决赛在二十八号。阿禾给他的功课只有一样：闭眼单脚站。他给自己也排了个「闭关三日」：四点四十起，五点到球馆，背一书包书深蹲，靠墙静蹲到蹲不住；脚踝不跳。还有一条：不许让阿禾知道。

头一天，他把《正常人体解剖学》和两本厚字典塞进书包，十来公斤，背着蹲：二十个一组，蹲了六组，一百二；再靠墙静蹲，三分十秒，蹲到腿抖得站不住。他拿粉笔写在看台底下的蓝软包上。

第二天两条大腿硬得像晾了一夜的油条，上厕所蹲不下去，得扶着墙；下楼梯一级一级，膝盖像生了锈。他想起不知哪儿看来的一句——疼，就是在长——又往书包里塞了一瓶水。蹲到一百个，腿就打摆子；他咬着牙，一组一组数到三百。静蹲两分零五。

第三天四点四十，他躺着量晨脉，照规矩发给阿禾：八十八。平时七十上下。腿是软的，下楼歇了两回。五点半，蹲到第二百个，手机一震：

「88？今天别练。」

他回了一个字：「好。」揣回兜里，蹲完了剩下的一百。静蹲一分二十。软包上三行粉笔字，一行比一行短，像三级往下走的台阶。

于是就有了那天夜里十一点的那一泡。他在厕所里站了一分钟，到底没忍住，出来跟室友说：「我的尿，是可乐色的。」

眼镜已经在搜了，脸色一点一点变了：「我查了。腿疼得碰不得、没劲、尿是可乐色——横纹肌溶解。没练过的肌肉猛加量，尤其是往下蹲那一段，肌纤维一根一根撕开，里头的肌红蛋白漏进血里；肾把它滤出来，尿就成了可乐色，滤多了，肾堵。马上去医院。」老蔡从上铺探出半个身子，一脸肃穆：「走火入魔。」

眼镜一边穿鞋一边给阿禾打电话。沈芒扑过去夺手机，腿一软，没夺着。

凌晨一点，急诊。大夫念化验单：「肌酸激酶，四万二。」沈芒问高吗。大夫说：「正常人一两百。」

阿禾赶来了，羽绒服底下露着一截睡裤，球鞋没穿袜子。她看了那袋盐水，看了那张单子，掏出本子写了一行，合上。一个字也没说。

住院三天。眼镜来了，摸出那本卷了边的《抱朴子内篇》：「葛洪那时候没有『走火入魔』这个词，倒有一句比它准：『力所不胜，而强举之，伤也。』」沈芒说：「我举得动啊。三百个呢。」眼镜拿指头点着那个「强」字：「你举得动的是那一下。伤不是哪一下伤的，是一天一天攒的。」

下午阿禾来了，坐在床尾，点着本子上那个八十八：「练完是挖坑。吃饱睡足，坑填平了，还多出一截——长的是那一截。晨脉高一截，就是坑还没填平。你一个坑没填，又往下挖了两天。」

二十八号半决赛，他在病床上看手机直播，针推赢了四分。镜头扫过替补席，十二只纸杯，他那只「0」也摆上了，扣着。散场以后，马小宝发来一张记分牌：「凑数的，决赛见。躺着可不算数。」

二十九日出院。阿禾在医院门口递给他一张纸，三条：晨脉回到七十以下，才许摸球；摸了球，只许罚球；十二月六号复查抽血。

等车的时候，沈芒憋不住了：「阿禾，你还生气呢？」

阿禾看着马路对面：「你练，我不气。练坏了，我也不气，谁都有头一回。」她停了一下，「我气的是，那天早上我问了你，你说好。」

他张了张嘴，什么也没说出来。

「你的数，我天天记。」阿禾说，「数是你自己报的。你报了实话，又不听，那我这本子，记的是什么？」

车来了。她先上了车，没回头。
story.en:
November 21st, round three of the group stage. On the bench stood a row of paper cups, mouths down, numbers written on the bottoms — Ahe's rule: whoever had played came off for a drink and turned his own cup over. Shen Mang sat in the stands on his crutches and counted twice: eleven. His cup, "0", hadn't been set out.

When the game broke up, Ma Xiaobao sauntered over and tapped his crutch with his shaker bottle: "Number Zero. A team registers twelve; one short and it can't enter — you're just here to make up the numbers." Neither of them mentioned that night in the rare-books room.

Not one word of it was wrong, which was why it hurt so much. But once the hurt passed, something in him quietly loosened: a number-filler, nobody watching, no need to step up to the free-throw line. The loosening startled him, and he hurried to push it back down.

That night Old Cai's phone dangled down from the top bunk, its screen stopped on a line: "The youth went into seclusion for three days and came out two realms higher."

The semifinal was on the 28th. Ahe had given him exactly one exercise: stand on one foot, eyes closed. He set himself a "three days of seclusion" too: up at four forty, in the gym by five, squats with a backpack full of books, wall sits until he couldn't hold them; no jumping, for the ankle. And one more rule: Ahe must not find out.

Day one, he stuffed *Normal Human Anatomy* and two fat dictionaries into his backpack, ten-odd kilos, and squatted under it: sets of twenty, six sets, a hundred and twenty; then a wall sit, three minutes ten, until his legs shook too hard to stand. He chalked it on the blue padding under the stands.

Day two both thighs were as stiff as fried dough sticks left out overnight; he couldn't squat over the toilet without holding the wall, and going downstairs one step at a time his knees felt rusted. He remembered a line he had read somewhere — pain means you're growing — and added a bottle of water to the backpack. By the hundredth squat his legs were trembling; he gritted his teeth and counted set by set to three hundred. Wall sit: two minutes five.

Day three, four forty, he took his morning pulse lying down and sent it to Ahe as the rule said: eighty-eight. Usually it was around seventy. His legs were weak; he rested twice on the way downstairs. At half past five, on his two hundredth squat, his phone buzzed:

"88? No training today."

He replied with one word: "OK." He put the phone back in his pocket and finished the last hundred. Wall sit: one minute twenty. Three lines of chalk on the padding, each shorter than the last, like three steps going down.

And that was how he came to that eleven o'clock pee. He stood in the bathroom for a minute, and in the end he couldn't keep it in; he came out and told his roommates, "My pee is the colour of cola."

Specs was already searching, and his face changed bit by bit: "I looked it up. Legs too sore to touch, no strength, cola-coloured urine — rhabdomyolysis. Untrained muscle, a sudden jump in load, especially the lowering part of a squat: the fibres tear one by one and the myoglobin inside leaks into the blood; the kidneys filter it out, which turns the urine cola-coloured, and filter too much and they clog. Hospital, now." Old Cai leaned half out of the top bunk, solemn: "Qi deviation."

Specs called Ahe while he pulled on his shoes. Shen Mang lunged for the phone, his legs gave way, and he missed.

One in the morning, the ER. The doctor read out the lab sheet: "Creatine kinase, forty-two thousand." Shen Mang asked if that was high. The doctor said, "A normal person's is one or two hundred."

Ahe arrived, pyjama bottoms showing under her down coat, sneakers with no socks. She looked at the bag of saline, looked at the lab sheet, took out her notebook, wrote a line and closed it. She didn't say a word.

Three days in hospital. Specs came and fished out his dog-eared copy of the Baopuzi, Inner Chapters: "Ge Hong didn't have the words 'qi deviation' back then, but he had a line that's more precise: 'When strength cannot bear it and one forces the lift, that is injury.'" Shen Mang said, "But I could lift it. Three hundred of them." Specs tapped the word "forces": "What you could lift was each single one. Injury doesn't come from any single one. It piles up, day by day."

In the afternoon Ahe came and sat at the foot of the bed, tapping the eighty-eight in her notebook: "Training digs a hole. Eat well, sleep enough, and the hole fills back up with a bit extra on top — that extra bit is what grows. When your morning pulse is up, the hole isn't filled yet. You didn't fill one hole, and then you dug down for two more days."

The semifinal on the 28th he watched on his phone from his hospital bed; Acupuncture and Tuina won by four. The camera swept the bench: twelve paper cups, and his "0" had been set out too, mouth down. After the game Ma Xiaobao sent a photo of the scoreboard: "Number-filler, see you in the final. Lying down doesn't count."

He was discharged on the 29th. At the hospital entrance Ahe handed him a sheet of paper with three rules: morning pulse back under seventy before he touched a ball; once he touched a ball, free throws only; blood test again on December 6th.

While they waited for the bus, Shen Mang couldn't hold it in: "Ahe, are you still angry?"

Ahe looked across the road: "You training doesn't make me angry. You training yourself into the ground doesn't either — everyone has a first time." She paused. "What makes me angry is that I asked you that morning, and you said OK."

He opened his mouth, and nothing came out.

"I write your numbers down every day," said Ahe. "The numbers are what you report yourself. If you report the truth and then don't listen, what is this notebook of mine keeping track of?"

The bus came. She got on first, and didn't look back.

exits.means: waits for the morning pulse to come down before touching the ball

refuse.zh: 晨脉还没回到七十以下。
refuse.en: The morning pulse isn't under seventy yet.

story.zh:
七十六，七十二。什么也不许干，只许吃、睡、躺着，他头一回知道歇着也要咬牙。十二月二日早上六点，他两根指头搭在腕子上数了两遍：六十九。他一骨碌坐起来，脑袋「咚」地撞在上铺床板上，捂着脑袋咧着嘴说：「出关了。」

阿禾回了一个字：「记。」

十二月七日，露天球场，北风刮得篮网横着飘，他十投二。夜里，学校表白墙出了一条决赛竞猜，两支队二十四个名字，各跟一个百分数。他划到最末一行：

「0号　沈芒（针推）　上场概率：1%」

底下点赞最多的评论：「那1%，是怕他哭。」

他盯着那个「1%」看了很久，倒觉得这个数挺好：一百回里有一回，就是说，还有一回。
story.en:
Seventy-six, seventy-two. Nothing allowed but eating, sleeping and lying down, and for the first time he learned that resting takes gritted teeth too. At six in the morning on December 2nd he laid two fingers on his wrist and counted twice: sixty-nine. He sat bolt upright, banged his head on the boards of the top bunk, and said through a grin, clutching his head: "Out of seclusion."

Ahe replied with one word: "Noted."

December 7th, the outdoor court, the north wind blowing the net sideways; he went two for ten. That night the school's confessions wall put up a poll for the final: twenty-four names from the two teams, each with a percentage. He scrolled to the last line:

"No. 0  Shen Mang (Acu-Tuina)  Chance of playing: 1%"

The most-liked comment below it: "That 1% is so he won't cry."

He stared at that "1%" for a long time, and decided it was a good number: one time in a hundred meant there was still one time.
